36 cases; each compares raw stdout bytes, raw stderr bytes and exit code against the oracle expectation. Result: 36/36 passed, 0 failed.
Per-case expected vs actual stdout/stderr/exit: evidence/differential-report.json and evidence/differential-report.txt.
Required items covered: --version; --version with a missing file (reads nothing); single file; multi-file incl. total line (both orders); empty file; missing trailing newline; \r and \t (plus \v/\f) whitespace; non-UTF-8 content; word spanning the 64 KiB read boundary (6 boundary cases: split word, separator at boundary, newline at boundary, all-ws chunk, 2-chunk word); missing file; missing+good (continue after error); good+missing; unknown option (--help, -x, with a file); no args.
Extended: directory operand (not-a-file); permission denied EACCES + continue; non-UTF-8 path echoed byte-for-byte; only-newlines; lone \r; whitespace-only; NUL bytes; ./ path echoed without normalisation; large 200k-line file; multi non-UTF-8 with total; U+3000 and U+00A0 bytes treated as NON-whitespace (byte-level, no Unicode segmentation). All PASS.

=== SPEC-UNDERDETERMINED (recorded, NOT scored as pass/fail) ===
1) Precedence when --version is combined with an unknown option (e.g. '--version -x'): SPEC gives no rule. Observed: usage error, exit 2.
2) The exact <description> text in error lines: SPEC uses a placeholder. Observed: Rust io::Error Display, e.g. 'No such file or directory (os error 2)', 'Permission denied (os error 13)'.
3) What the 'total' line sums when some operands fail: SPEC does not state. Observed: sums readable operands only and still emits total when >1 FILE was given.
4) Empty-string arg / lone '-' / a file name beginning with '-': undefined. Observed: '' -> open error exit 1; '-' -> usage exit 2; '--x' -> usage exit 2.
These are ambiguities of the specification, not implementation defects; they are excluded from the verdict rather than silently scored.

=== NOT COVERED (explicit, with reason) ===
- stdin / TTY / '-' as stdin: SPEC defines no stdin input path (outside contract).
- Files larger than ~600 KiB / multi-GiB: streaming is O(1) memory and all 64 KiB boundary logic is covered; only up to 200000 lines (~600 KB) and 2x64 KiB blocks were exercised.
- Concurrent truncation/rename of an operand between open and read (TOCTOU): not in SPEC.
- SIGPIPE / closed stdout and stdout-vs-stderr interleaving order: not specified.
- EIO/ENOSPC and signal-driven exits: not deterministically reachable in this sandbox.
- Non-Linux / Windows path semantics: SPEC is byte-level; harness is Linux-only.
- Locale/Unicode word segmentation beyond the whitespace byte set: SPEC forbids Unicode segmentation; U+3000 and U+00A0 were spot-checked as non-whitespace bytes.
